content: Efavirenz interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through the cytochrome P450 system (CYP3A4, CYP2C9/10, CYP2B6, etc.). Below are the detailed interactions and clinical considerations for each drug: 1. Efavirenz and Marijuana: Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of marijuana by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Efavirenz and Mavorixafor: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc closely in patients with risk factors, and dose reduction or discontinuation of Mavorixafor may be necessary. 3. Efavirenz and Meclizine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor for excessive sedation. 4. Efavirenz and Medroxyprogesterone: Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Efavirenz and Mefloquine: Efavirenz reduces mefloquine levels via CYP3A4 induction and both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor QTc. 6. Efavirenz and Meloxicam: Efavirenz increases meloxicam levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Efavirenz and Meperidine: Efavirenz decreases meperidine levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially increasing toxic metabolite formation. Use caution and monitor. 8. Efavirenz and Mestranol: Efavirenz reduces mestranol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Efavirenz and Metaxalone: Efavirenz decreases metaxalone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 10. Efavirenz and Methadone: Efavirenz reduces methadone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Efavirenz and Methohexital: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor for excessive sedation. 12. Efavirenz and Methsuximide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 13. Efavirenz and Methylprednisolone: Efavirenz decreases methylprednisolone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Efavirenz and Midazolam: Efavirenz reduces midazolam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 15. Efavirenz and Intranasal Midazolam: Both drugs may increase toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Concomitant use with CNS depressants (e.g., barbiturates, alcohol) may increase risks of hypoventilation, airway obstruction, or apnea. 16. Efavirenz and Mifepristone: Efavirenz induces CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 but also inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro, potentially affecting mifepristone levels. Mifepristone inhibits CYP2B6, increasing efavirenz exposure. Use caution and monitor. 17. Efavirenz and Mirtazapine: Efavirenz reduces mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 induction, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 18. Efavirenz and Mitotane: Mitotane decreases efavirenz levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor and adjust dosages as needed. 19. Efavirenz and Modafinil: Efavirenz reduces modafinil levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 20. Efavirenz and Molindone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 21. Efavirenz and Nafcillin: Nafcillin decreases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 induction. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may increase metabolism of efavirenz. Use caution and monitor. 22. Efavirenz and Naldemedine: Efavirenz reduces naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling suggests decreased exposure to naldemedine with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. The clinical consequence is unknown. Use caution and monitor. 23. Efavirenz and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Efavirenz and Nelfinavir: Efavirenz reduces nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 25. Efavirenz and Nicardipine: Efavirenz reduces nicardipine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 26. Efavirenz and Nifedipine: Efavirenz reduces nifedipine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Efavirenz and Nilotinib: Efavirenz reduces nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 28. Efavirenz and Nirmatrelvir: Nirmatrelvir increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Efavirenz and Nitrous Oxide: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 30. Efavirenz and Norgestrel: Efavirenz reduces norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider additional barrier contraceptive methods. 31. Efavirenz and Nortriptyline: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 32. Efavirenz and Octreotide: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 33. Efavirenz and Ofloxacin: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 34. Efavirenz and Olanzapine: Both prolong the QTc interval. Limited data suggest olanzapine may rarely cause significant QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 35. Efavirenz and Oliceridine: Efavirenz reduces oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Consider increasing the oliceridine dose if coadministered. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 36. Efavirenz and Olodaterol: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 37. Efavirenz and Omeprazole: Efavirenz increases omeprazole levels via CYP2C19 inhibition but decreases them via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 38. Efavirenz and Ondansetron: Efavirenz reduces ondansetron levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 39. Efavirenz and Opicapone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 40. Efavirenz and Orlistat: Orlistat reduces efavirenz levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 41. Efavirenz and Osilodrostat: Efavirenz reduces osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Efavirenz and Ospemifene: Efavirenz reduces ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 43. Efavirenz and Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin increases efavirenz levels. Monitor for ECG changes if coadministered with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 44. Efavirenz and Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine reduces efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 45. Efavirenz and Oxycodone: Efavirenz reduces oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 46. Efavirenz and Palbociclib: Efavirenz reduces palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Efavirenz and Paricalcitol: Efavirenz reduces paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 48. Efavirenz and Pasireotide: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 49. Efavirenz and Pazopanib: Efavirenz reduces pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 50. Efavirenz and Perphenazine: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 51. Efavirenz and Phenytoin: Efavirenz increases phenytoin levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition, while phenytoin reduces efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for reduced efavirenz efficacy and phenytoin plasma concentrations. 52. Efavirenz and Pimavanserin: Efavirenz reduces pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy and consider increasing its dosage. 53. Efavirenz and Pimozide: Efavirenz reduces pimozide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 54. Efavirenz and Piroxicam: Efavirenz increases piroxicam levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 55. Efavirenz and Pitolisant: Efavirenz reduces pitolisant levels via CYP3A4 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce pitolisant dosage by half if the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued. 56. Efavirenz and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Efavirenz reduces polatuzumab vedotin levels by decreasing unconjugated MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate). Use caution and monitor. 57. Efavirenz and Prednisolone/Prednisone: Efavirenz reduces prednisolone and prednisone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 58. Efavirenz and Primaquine: Efavirenz reduces primaquine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 59. Efavirenz and Prochlorperazine: Both decrease the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 60. Efavirenz and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, Natural): Efavirenz reduces progesterone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 61. Efavirenz and Proguanil: Efavirenz reduces proguanil levels by an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing the active metabolite. Use caution and monitor. 62. Efavirenz and Promethazine: Both decrease the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 63. Efavirenz and Protriptyline: Both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 64. Efavirenz and Quazepam: Efavirenz reduces quazepam levels via CYP3A4 induction, while quazepam increases efavirenz levels via CYP2B6 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 65. Efavirenz and Quetiapine: Efavirenz reduces quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 66. Efavirenz and Quinidine: Efavirenz reduces quinidine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 67. Efavirenz and Ramelteon: Efavirenz increases ramelteon levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 68. Efavirenz and Repaglinide: Efavirenz reduces repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 69. Efavirenz and Resmetirom: Efavirenz increases resmetirom levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce resmetirom dosage with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 70. Efavirenz and Ribociclib: Efavirenz reduces ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers. 71. Efavirenz and Rifabutin/Rifampin: Both drugs reduce efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 induction. Use caution and monitor. 72. Efavirenz and Riociguat: Efavirenz reduces riociguat levels via CYP3A4 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 73. Efavirenz and Risperidone: Efavirenz reduces risperidone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 74. Efavirenz and Ritonavir: Efavirenz reduces ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 75. Efavirenz and Rivaroxaban: Efavirenz reduces rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 76. Efavirenz and Roflumilast: Efavirenz reduces roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 induction. Coadministration is not recommended due to reduced therapeutic effectiveness. 77. Efavirenz and Romidepsin: Efavirenz reduces romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 78. Efavirenz and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases efavirenz levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust dosages of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated.
